items.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...I knew Chuck. But it was Gap’s record.

ctx.x: I just think that’s fair. I think it’s fair to the artist, and we let the artist know we pulled the review, it got a one star review. Sometimes we’ll even, if we feel, you know, there are times that I love things and other people don’t. And I can’t figure out why. So we may take it and give it to another reviewer and see what they think of it. And then from there, at that point we’ll say we’re not going to hurt this person’s career at this point. If they become famous then we have to really review it.

I don’t know why, you just said something that reminded me, this was before your tenure, I think it was the late 70s. I remember a review by a release by Gap Mangione. And I sort of knew Gap, not at the time, but I knew Chuck. But it was Gap’s record. And apparently on the liner notes the writer was celebrating the chemistry of the trio. So the reviewer wrote: “If this is chemistry then women are wearing concrete underwear.” And I was like, “Did I just read that?” And I’m not sure I got the exact — but that was…

There are times where an editor will say, or I’ll say if it comes up to me, I end up being the ombudsman for the company. You know people can’t decide what to do with things or there’s an argument whether we should do this or do that, the editors will come to me with that kind of problem and then we’ll work out a solution. But yeah, if we think the writer is being unfair, and there are times where it slips through because it doesn’t seem that way to us, and then later on I’ll go yeah, right, if the artist comes —…
